pairs.fullEnglish: And Jacob dwelt in the land of his father's sojourning, in the land of Canaan.

These are the generations of Jacob: Joseph was seventeen years old (when) he was tending the flock with his brothers, and he was growing up with the sons of Bilhah and with the sons of Zilpah, his father's wives. And Joseph brought the evil report about them to their father.
And his brothers saw that their father loved him more than all his brothers, and they hated him and were unwilling to speak peaceably with him.
And Joseph dreamed a dream and told his brothers, and they hated him still more.
And he said to them, ‘Hear now this dream that I have dreamed.’
‘And behold, we were binding sheaves in the field, and behold, my sheaf rose and also stood upright; and behold, your sheaves were surrounding it and bowing down to my sheaf.’

And his brothers said to him, ‘Do you imagine that you will indeed reign over us, or do you suppose that you will exercise dominion over us?’ And they hated him still more because of his dreams and because of his words.
And he dreamed yet another dream and related it to his brothers, and said, ‘Behold, I have dreamed another dream, and behold, the sun and the moon and eleven stars were bowing down to me.’

And he related it to his father and to his brothers; and his father rebuked him and said to him, ‘What is this dream that you have dreamed? Shall I and your mother and your brothers really come to bow down to you upon the ground?’
And his brothers were jealous of him, but his father kept the matter in mind.
And his brothers went to tend their father's flock in Shechem.
And Israel said to Joseph, ‘Are not your brothers tending the flock in Shechem? Come, and I will send you to them.’ And he said to him, ‘Here I am.’
And a man found him, and behold, he was wandering in the field; and the man asked him, saying, ‘What are you seeking?’
And he said, ‘I am seeking my brothers. Tell me now where they are tending the flock.’
And the man said, ‘They have departed from here, for I heard them saying, “Let us go to דֹתָן.”’ And Joseph went after his brothers and found them in דֹתָן.
And they saw him from afar, before he came near them, and they plotted against him to kill him.
And they said, each to his brother, ‘Behold, that master of dreams is coming.’
‘And now, come, let us kill him and throw him into one of the pits, and let us say, “An evil beast has devoured him”; and we shall see what will become of his dreams in the end.’
And Reuben heard and rescued him from their hands, and said, ‘Let us not take his life.’
And Reuben said to them, ‘Do not shed blood. Throw him into this pit that is in the wilderness, but do not lay a hand on him’—in order to rescue him from their hands, to return him to his father.
And they took him and threw him into the pit; and the pit was empty, with no water in it.
And Judah said to his brothers, ‘What monetary benefit shall we gain if we kill our brother and cover up his blood?’
‘Come, let us sell him to the Arabs, and let our hand not be against him, for he is our brother, our flesh.’ And his brothers accepted his words.
And Reuben returned to the pit, and behold, Joseph was not in the pit; and he tore his garments.
And he returned to his brothers and said, ‘The young man is not here; and I—where am I to go?’
And they took Joseph's tunic and slaughtered a male goat, and dipped the tunic in the blood.
And he recognized it and said, ‘My son's tunic! An evil beast has devoured him; Joseph has surely been killed.’
And Jacob tore his garments and bound sackcloth about his loins, and mourned for his son many days.
And it happened at that time that Judah went down from his brothers and turned aside to an Adullamite man whose name was חִירָה.
And Judah saw there the daughter of a merchant man whose name was שׁוּעַ; and he took her as his wife and went in to her.
And she conceived and bore a son, and he called his name עֵר.
And she conceived again and bore a son, and she called his name אוֹנָן.
And she again bore a son, and she called his name שֵׁלָה; and he was in כְּזִיב when she bore him.
And Judah took a wife for עֵר, his firstborn, and her name was Tamar.
And עֵר, Judah's firstborn, was evil before יְיָ, and יְיָ put him to death.
And Judah said to אוֹנָן, ‘Go in to your brother's wife, marry her as your brother's widow, and raise up offspring for your brother.’
And what he did was evil before יְיָ, and He put him also to death.

And Judah said to Tamar, his daughter-in-law, ‘Remain a widow in your father's house until my son שֵׁלָה grows up’; for he said, ‘Lest he too die like his brothers.’ And Tamar went and dwelt in her father's house.
And many days passed, and the daughter of שׁוּעַ, Judah's wife, died; and Judah was comforted and went up to the shearers of his flock, he and his friend חִירָה the Adullamite, to תִּמְנָת.
And Tamar was told, saying, ‘Behold, your father-in-law is going up to תִּמְנָת to shear his flock.’
And Judah saw her and considered her a prostitute, because she had covered her face.
And he turned aside to her by the road and said, ‘Come now, let me go in to you,’ for he did not know that she was his daughter-in-law. And she said, ‘What will you give me if you go in to me?’
And he said, ‘I will send a kid of the goats from the flock.’ And she said, ‘If you give a pledge until you send it.’
And she arose and went away, and removed her veil from herself and put on the garments of her widowhood.
And Judah sent the kid of the goats by the hand of his Adullamite friend, to take the pledge from the woman's hand; but he did not find her.
And Judah said, ‘Let her keep it, lest we become a laughingstock. Behold, I sent this kid, but you did not find her.’
And Judah recognized them and said, ‘She is in the right; she is pregnant by me, because I did not give her to my son שֵׁלָה.’ And he did not again have relations with her.
And it happened at the time of her giving birth that, behold, there were twins in her womb.
And it happened as she was giving birth that one put out a hand; and the midwife took a scarlet thread and tied it on his hand, saying, ‘This one came out first.’
And afterward his brother came out, on whose hand was the scarlet thread; and he called his name זָרַח.
And Joseph was brought down to Egypt, and Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh, chief of the executioners, an Egyptian man, bought him from the hand of the Arabs who had brought him down there.
And the Word of יְיָ was Joseph's help, and he was a successful man; and he was in the house of his Egyptian master.
And his master saw that the Word of יְיָ was his help, and that everything he did, יְיָ made successful in his hand.
And Joseph found favor in his eyes and served him, and he appointed him over his house; and all that he had he entrusted to his hand.

And it happened, from the time that he appointed him over his house and over all that he had, that יְיָ blessed the Egyptian's house because of Joseph; and the blessing of יְיָ was upon all that he had, in the house and in the field.
And it happened after these things that his master's wife raised her eyes toward Joseph and said, ‘Lie with me.’
‘He is not greater in this house than I, and he has withheld nothing from me except you, because you are his wife. And how could I do this great evil and incur guilt before יְיָ?’
And it happened, as she spoke with Joseph day after day, that he did not accept her words, to lie beside her, to be with her.
And it happened on this day that he entered the house to examine his account books, and none of the men of the household was there in the house.
And she seized him by his garment, saying, ‘Lie with me’; and he left his garment in her hand and fled and went out into the street.
And it happened, when she saw that he had left his garment in her hand and had fled into the street,
that she called to the men of her household and said to them, saying, ‘See, he has brought us a Hebrew man to mock us. He came in to me to lie with me, and I cried out in a loud voice.’
‘And it happened, when he heard that I raised my voice and cried out, that he left his garment beside me and fled and went out into the street.’
And she laid his garment beside her until his master came into his house.
And she spoke to him according to these words, saying, ‘The Hebrew slave whom you brought us came in to me to mock me.’
‘And it happened, when I raised my voice and cried out, that he left his garment beside me and fled into the street.’
And it happened, when his master heard the words of his wife that she spoke to him, saying, ‘Your slave did these things to me,’ that his anger grew fierce.
And Joseph's master took him and placed him in the prison, the place where the king's prisoners were confined; and he was there in the prison.
And the Word of יְיָ was Joseph's help, and extended kindness to him and granted him favor in the eyes of the chief of the prison.
And the chief of the prison placed in Joseph's hand all the prisoners who were in the prison; and everything that they did there was done at his word.
The chief of the prison saw no fault at all in his hand, because the Word of יְיָ was his help; and whatever he did, יְיָ made successful.
And it happened after these things that the cupbearer of the king of Egypt and the baker offended against their master, the king of Egypt.
And Pharaoh was angry with his two officers, with the chief of the cupbearers and with the chief of the bakers.
And he put them in custody in the house of the chief of the executioners, in the prison, the place where Joseph was confined.
And the chief of the executioners appointed Joseph to be with them, and he served them; and they were in custody for some days.

And both of them dreamed a dream, each his own dream, on one night, each according to the interpretation of his dream—the cupbearer and the baker of the king of Egypt, who were confined in the prison.
And Joseph came to them in the morning and saw them, and behold, they were dejected.
And he asked Pharaoh's officers who were with him in custody in his master's house, saying, ‘Why are your faces troubled today?’
And they said to him, ‘We have dreamed a dream, and there is no one to interpret it.’ And Joseph said to them, ‘Are not the interpretations of dreams from before יְיָ? Tell me now.’
And the chief of the cupbearers related his dream to Joseph and said to him, ‘In my dream, behold, a vine was before me.’
‘And on the vine were three branches; and when it sprouted, it put forth buds and blossomed, and its clusters ripened into grapes.’
‘And Pharaoh's cup was in my hand, and I took the grapes and pressed them into Pharaoh's cup, and I placed the cup upon Pharaoh's hand.’
And Joseph said to him, ‘This is its interpretation: the three branches are three days.’
‘Only remember me when it goes well with you, and do kindness with me now, and mention me before Pharaoh, and bring me out of this prison.’
‘For I was indeed stolen from the land of the Hebrews, and here also I did nothing for which they should have placed me in the prison.’
‘And in the uppermost basket was some of every kind of Pharaoh's food, the work of a baker; and the birds were eating them from the basket above my head.’
And Joseph answered and said, ‘This is its interpretation: the three baskets are three days.’
And he restored the chief of the cupbearers to his cupbearing, and he placed the cup upon Pharaoh's hand.
And the chief of the cupbearers did not remember Joseph, and he forgot him.
And he said to him, ‘Go now, see how your brothers are and how the flock is, and bring me back word.’ And he sent him from the plain of Hebron, and he came to Shechem.
And Midianite men, merchants, passed by, and they drew Joseph out and brought him up from the pit, and they sold Joseph to the Arabs for twenty pieces of silver; and they brought Joseph to Egypt.

qualifications.he: בתחילת המשפט נזכרים במפורש סוחרים מדיינים; אחר כך באים פעלים ברבים בלי ציון מחודש של שם העושים. התרגום שומר את הרצף ואת כינוי הגוף הם, ואינו מוסיף שהאחים הם שהוציאו את יוסף ומכרוהו. אין בכך הכרעה עצמאית כיצד ליישב את כל תיאורי ההעלאה, המכירה וההבאה למצרים שבפסוקים השונים.
qualifications.en: Midianite merchants are expressly named at the start of the sentence; the following verbs are plural without freshly naming their actors. The translation preserves that sequence and the pronoun they; it does not insert the brothers as those who drew Joseph out and sold him. This does not independently resolve how all the accounts of drawing up, selling, and bringing to Egypt in the different verses fit together.
qualifications.anchor: וּנְגִידוּ וְאַסִּיקוּ יָת יוֹסֵף מִן גֻּבָּא וְזַבִּינוּ יָת יוֹסֵף

pairs.fullEnglish: And all his sons and all his daughters arose to comfort him, but he refused to receive consolation, and said, ‘For I shall go down to my son, mourning, to Sheol.’ And his father wept for him.

qualifications.he: הגוף מתרגם את הקריאה לות: אל בני. המקור מספק גם את החלופה שבסוגריים על: על בני. לפי החלופה הזאת ניתן להבין את הירידה לשאול כאבל על הבן, בלי האמירה אל בני. שתי הקריאות נשמרות כאן; לא נקבעת עדיפות נוסח.
qualifications.en: The body translates the reading לות: to my son. The source also supplies parenthetical על: over or concerning my son. Under that alternative, the descent to Sheol can be understood as mourning for the son, without saying to my son. Both supplied readings are preserved here; no textual priority is asserted.

pairs.fullEnglish: And the Midianites sold him into Egypt, to Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh, chief of the executioners.

And אוֹנָן knew that the offspring would not be called by his name; and whenever he went in to his brother's wife, he would corrupt his way upon the ground, so as not to raise up offspring for his brother.

qualifications.he: הביטוי משחית את דרכו על הארץ בא כאן בתוך תיאור הביאה אל אשת אחיו. בהקשר הזה הוא מתאר קלקול מכוון של דרך הביאה כדי שלא להקים זרע לאחיו, כפי שמפורש בסוף הפסוק. נשמרת לשון הדרך של המקור; אין מוסיפים שם של חומר או פירוט גופני שאינם נקובים בו.
qualifications.en: Corrupt his way upon the ground occurs within the account of intercourse with his brother's wife. In this context it describes deliberately frustrating the course of intercourse so as not to raise offspring for his brother, as the verse expressly states. The source's euphemistic way wording is retained; no substance or more specific physical procedure absent from its wording is named.

pairs.fullEnglish: And he said, ‘What pledge shall I give you?’ And she said, ‘Your ring and your wrap and your staff that is in your hand.’ And he gave them to her and went in to her, and she conceived by him.

qualifications.he: שושיפך מתורגם במונח הכללי מעטפתך, כלומר בגד התעטפות. אין כאן תרגום של פתיל או חוט, ואין קביעה של חומר הבגד או צורתו המדויקת.
qualifications.en: שושיפך is translated by the general garment term your wrap, a garment worn as a covering. It is not rendered as a cord or thread, and no precise material or cut is asserted.

pairs.fullEnglish: And he returned to Judah and said, ‘I did not find her; and the men of the place also said, “There is no prostitute here.”’

qualifications.he: זונה מתרגם כאן באופן כללי ולפי ההקשר את הכינוי מקדשתא, החוזר מדברי אנשי המקום. אין בכך קביעה שהכינוי זהה בכל גווניו לנפקת ברא, ואין ייחוס של תפקיד פולחני מסוים לאישה.
qualifications.en: Prostitute renders the repeated local designation מקדשתא in general contextual terms. It does not assert complete equivalence in nuance with נפקת ברא or assign the woman a particular cultic office.

pairs.fullEnglish: And it happened after about three months that Judah was told, saying, ‘Tamar, your daughter-in-law, has engaged in illicit intercourse, and behold, she is also pregnant from illicit intercourse.’ And Judah said, ‘Bring her out, and let her be burned.’
She was being brought out, and she sent to her father-in-law, saying, ‘By the man to whom these belong I am pregnant.’ And she said, ‘Recognize now whose are this ring and wrap and staff.’

qualifications.he: שושיפא מתורגם במונח הבגד הכללי מעטפת, כבהופעתו בפסוק יח; אין הכוונה לתרגום חוט או פתיל, ואין קביעה של סוג הבגד המדויק או חומרו.
qualifications.en: שושיפא is rendered by the general garment term wrap, as in verse 18; it is not a translation as a thread or cord and does not specify the garment's exact subtype or material.

pairs.fullEnglish: And he left all that he had in Joseph's hand, and with Joseph there he concerned himself with nothing except the bread that he ate. And Joseph was handsome in form and fair in appearance.
And he refused and said to his master's wife, ‘Behold, with me here, my master does not concern himself with what is in the house, and all that he has he has entrusted to my hand.’
‘At the end of three days Pharaoh will remove your head from you and suspend you on a gibbet, and the birds will eat your flesh from you.’

qualifications.he: יתלה אותך על מתקן תלייה הוא תרגום כללי של יצלוב על צליבא: תלייה או הצבה של הגוף על מתקן. הפסוק אומר בנפרד שפרעה יסיר את ראשו. אין כאן קביעה של צורת המתקן, אמצעי החיבור אליו או הליך ביצוע מעבר לנאמר במפורש.
qualifications.en: Suspend you on a gibbet is a general rendering of יצלוב על צליבא: suspension or mounting of the body on an execution or display structure. The verse separately says that Pharaoh will remove his head. No particular shape, means of attachment, or procedure beyond what is expressly stated is asserted.

pairs.fullEnglish: And the chief of the bakers he suspended on a gibbet, as Joseph had interpreted to them.

qualifications.he: תלה על מתקן תלייה הוא תרגום כללי של צלב, בהתאם ללשון יצלוב על צליבא שבפסוק יט. אין כאן תוספת של צורת מתקן מסוימת או שיטת חיבור וביצוע שאינן מפורשות במקור.
qualifications.en: Suspended on a gibbet renders צלב generally, corresponding to יצלוב על צליבא in verse 19. It adds no specific structure shape, means of attachment, or execution technique not expressed in the source.

pairs.fullEnglish: Yet I destroyed the Amorite from before them, whose height was like the height of cedars and who was strong as oaks; I destroyed his fruit above and his roots below.
And I brought you up from the land of Egypt and led you in the wilderness forty years, to inherit the land of the Amorite.
And I raised up some of your sons as prophets and some of your young men as teachers. Is this not indeed so, children of Israel? says יְיָ.
For my mouth speaks truth, and wickedness is far removed from my lips.
All the utterances of my mouth are in righteousness, and there is no twisting or crookedness in them.
They are all clear to a person who understands, and upright to those who desire knowledge.
Accept discipline and not silver, and choose knowledge for yourselves rather than refined gold.
For wisdom is better than precious stones, and nothing at all compares with it.
I, wisdom, dwell with prudence; knowledge and thoughtful purpose I find.
But you led your teachers astray with wine, and you commanded the prophets, saying, 'Do not prophesy any prophecy.'
Behold, I am bringing distress upon you and pressing you in your own place, as a cart loaded with sheaves presses down.
The one who holds the bow will not stand; the one swift on his feet will not escape, and the rider of horses will not save his own life.
Fear of יְיָ hates evil; pride and haughtiness, an evil way and a perverse mouth, I hate.
For thoughtful purpose, counsel, understanding, and might are mine.
Because of me kings reign, and I anoint rulers in righteousness.
Even the stouthearted among the mighty men will flee naked, without weapons, on that day, says יְיָ.
Accept this pronouncement that יְיָ has decreed against you, house of Israel, against all the families that I brought up from the land of Egypt, saying:
In you alone have I taken delight, out of all the families of the earth; therefore I will visit upon you all your sins.
Will two walk together unless they have met up?
Will a lion roar in the forest when it has no prey? Will a young lion raise its voice from its lair unless it has caught something?
I love those who love me, and those who come early to me will find me.
I walk in the ways of righteousness, amid the paths of judgment,
so that I may cause those who love me to inherit many years, and I will fill their treasuries.
If a horn is sounded in a city outside its appointed time, will the people in it not tremble? If calamity occurs in a city, has it not been done from before יְיָ?
A lion has roared—who will not fear? יְיָ אֱלֹהִים has spoken—who will not receive prophecy?

Proclaim over the palaces in Ashdod and over the palaces in the land of Egypt, and say: Gather upon the mountains of Samaria, and see the many disturbances within her, and those who are oppressed within her.
They do not know how to act according to the Torah, says יְיָ—those who fill their treasuries with robbery and plunder in their palaces.
And before the world I was established, from its beginning, and before the earth came to be.
Before the depths came to be I was born, and before the mighty springs of water came to be.
Of old, before the mountains were sunk in place, and before the hills, I was built.
Before He made the earth and the watercourses, and the first dust of the inhabited world.
Therefore thus says יְיָ אֱלֹהִים: Severe distress is coming upon the land; your might will be removed from you, and your palaces will be plundered.

Thus says יְיָ: As a shepherd rescues from a lion's mouth two legs or the cartilage of an ear, so will the children of Israel be rescued, those who dwell in Samaria in the strength of their rule and put their trust in Damascus.
Receive this and bear witness in the house of Jacob, says יְיָ אֱלֹהִים אֱלֹהֵי צְבָאוֹת.
And when He made the clouds firm above, and when He strengthened the springs of the deep;
And now, children, listen to me; happy is the one who keeps my ways.
On bedding taken in pledge they recline beside all their altars, and wine obtained by extortion they drink in the house of their idols.

qualifications.he: מצעים הוא כאן שם רחב לחפצים שעליהם מסבים ושנלקחו במשכון. אין הנוסח מכריע אם היו אלה כיסויים, כלי משכב או ספות, ואינו מפרט את חומרם או את מבנם. מסחרין מתורגם לפי פעולת ההסבה עליהם; אין החלפה אוטומטית בבגדים מן הפסוק העברי.
qualifications.en: 'Bedding' is used broadly for the pledged objects on which they recline. It does not determine whether these were covers, bedding, or couches, or specify their material or construction. מְסַחֲרִין is rendered as reclining on them; garments have not been imported from the Hebrew verse.

pairs.fullEnglish: Wealth and honor are mine—possessions, fortune, and righteousness.

qualifications.he: מזלא מתורגם כאן במובן הרחב של מזל או גורל. אין לידו במקור תואר מפורש של טוב, ואין הניסוח מכריע אם יש למילה גם גוון אסטרולוגי. אין מחליפים אותה בעושר מתמיד מן הפסוק העברי.
qualifications.en: מַזָלָא is rendered broadly as 'fortune,' without adding an explicit 'good' or deciding whether the word also has an astrological coloring. It is not replaced by the Hebrew verse's enduring wealth.

pairs.fullEnglish: For on the day when I visit Israel's sins upon him, I will also visit punishment upon those who serve the altars in Bais El; the horns of the altar will be cut off and will fall to the ground.

qualifications.he: עובדי המזבחות מתאר את עבודת הפולחן הקשורה למזבחות, לפי פלחין לאגוריא. אין בניסוח הכרעה שהמזבח עצמו נחשב אלוה, ואין צמצום של הלמ״ד לציון מקום בלבד. הפקידה היא במפורש על האנשים העובדים; כריתת קרנות המזבח ונפילתן הן תיאור נוסף.
qualifications.en: 'Those who serve the altars' describes cultic service related to the altars, following פָּלְחִין לֶאֱגוֹרַיָא. It does not determine that an altar is itself treated as a deity, or reduce the preposition to location alone. The visitation is expressly upon the people performing that service; the cutting off and falling of the altar's horns are an additional statement.
qualifications.anchor: וְאַסְעַר עַל דְפָלְחִין לֶאֱגוֹרַיָא בְּבֵית אֵל

pairs.fullEnglish: I was rejoicing in His inhabited earth, and my praises were among human beings.

qualifications.he: שבוחי נשמר כלשון שבח של המדברת, ובבני נשא מתורגם באופן רחב בין בני האדם. אין בכך קביעה אם השבח נאמר בפיהם או מכוון אליהם, ואין הופכים את הצלע לאמירה מפורשת על הנאה מבני אדם. השמחה המפורשת בצלע הראשונה היא בתבל ארצו.
qualifications.en: שִׁבּוּחֵי retains the speaker's praise language, and בִּבְנֵי נָשָׁא is rendered broadly as 'among human beings.' This does not determine whether they voice the praise or are its object, and does not convert the clause into an explicit statement of delight in humanity. The first limb expressly locates rejoicing in His inhabited earth.

pairs.fullEnglish: A place of escape will be lost to the swift; the strong will not make his strength prevail, and the mighty man will not save his own life.

qualifications.he: בית עיקוקי מתורגם באופן רחב כמקום מפלט, על פי מקומו ברצף של אובדן הצלה גם לקל ברגליו, לחזק ולגיבור. אין כאן זיהוי של אתר, דרך מילוט או מבנה מסוים, ואין הכרעה בפרטי צורת הביטוי הנדיר מעבר לתפקידו זה במשפט.
qualifications.en: בֵּית עֵיקוּקֵי is rendered broadly as a place of escape in the sequence denying deliverance even to the swift, strong, and mighty. No particular location, escape route, or structure is identified, and no more exact account of the rare expression's form is claimed.

pairs.fullEnglish: God created me at the beginning of His creation, and before His works, from the outset.
And I will strike the winter house together with the summer house; the houses adorned with elephant ivory will perish, and many houses will come to an end, says יְיָ.

qualifications.he: המקור מציין בתי פאר שיש בהם עיטור בשן פיל. הניסוח האנגלי אינו קובע אם השן שימשה לוחות, ציפוי או שיבוץ, ואינו טוען שהבתים עצמם נבנו כולם משן.
qualifications.en: The source describes houses embellished with elephant ivory. The English does not determine whether the ivory formed panels, facing, or inlay, and does not claim that the houses were built entirely of ivory.

pairs.fullEnglish: They treat the poor man's head with contempt in the dust of the earth, and pervert the judgment of the needy; a man and his father go to the same young woman, in order to profane My holy name.

qualifications.he: לשון הביזוי נשמרת יחד עם ראש העני ועפר הארץ. הניסוח בעפר משמר את תמונת ההשפלה ואינו קובע שהעני נרמס בגופו, או מתאר פעולה גופנית מסוימת. אין כאן החלפה של בי״ת במילת השוואה מפורשת.
qualifications.en: The rendering retains contempt, the poor man's head, and the dust of the earth. 'In the dust' preserves the image of humiliation without asserting literal trampling or a particular physical action. It does not turn the source preposition into an explicit word of comparison.

pairs.fullEnglish: Because of me great men become great, and so do governors—all of them judges of uprightness.

qualifications.he: המילים and so do באנגלית ממשיכות אל הסרכים את הנשוא מתרברבין שבצלע הקודמת; אין פועל שני מפורש במקור. סרכי מתורגם כמושלים או ממונים. כלהון נשמר ככינוי כולל, בלי לקבוע שהוא מוציא את הגדולים, הנקראים רַבְרְבָנֵי בתחילת הפסוק, מתחולתו.
qualifications.en: English 'and so do' carries over מִתְרַבְרְבִין from the preceding coordinated clause; the source has no second explicit verb. סַרְכֵי denotes governors or officials. 'All of them' retains the collective pronoun without claiming that it excludes the great men named at the start of the verse.

pairs.fullEnglish: When He established the heavens, I was there, and when He traced a circle over the surface of the deep.

qualifications.he: ועד מצטרף למסגרת הזמן הפותחת בכד ולתיאור נוכחות החכמה. כאשר באנגלית מציין כאן את נוכחותה בזמן חקיקת המעגל; אין בכך הכרעה אם עד מדגיש גם פרק זמן המגיע עד לאותה פעולה. אין אמירה שנוכחותה חדלה אחריה. חוגתא נשאר מעגל, ולא מוחלף בשמים או בכיפה.
qualifications.en: וְעַד continues the temporal frame opened by כַּד and the account of wisdom's presence. English 'when' gives its presence at the tracing of the circle without settling whether עַד also emphasizes an interval reaching that act. It does not assert that its presence ceased afterward. חוּגְתָא remains a circle, not heavens or a vault.
qualifications.anchor: וְעַד חָג חוּגְתָא עַל אַפֵּי תְהוֹמָא

pairs.fullEnglish: and when He set the sea its boundary, and the waters do not cross it, (and when) He laid the foundations of the earth.

qualifications.he: וכד מופיע בסוגריים במקור, והסוגריים נשמרים גם באנגלית. לא נקבע כאן אם זהו נוסח עיקרי, חלופה או תוספת מסומנת. הכינוי ליה נשמר באנגלית כ־it בהמשך לתיאור תחום הים; אין מוסיפים לו אמירה או מצווה שאינה כתובה. ההערה משמרת את מצב הנוסח ואינה מכריעה את תולדותיו.
qualifications.en: The source prints וְכַד in parentheses, and the English retains them. No decision is made that these are main wording, a variant, or a marked addition. לֵיהּ remains English 'it' in the context of the sea's boundary; no unexpressed utterance or command is added. This preserves the supplied textual presentation without adjudicating its history.
qualifications.anchor: וּמַיָא לָא עָבְרִין לֵיהּ (וְכַד) שָׂם שַׁתְאַסַיָא דְאַרְעָא

pairs.fullEnglish: Thus says יְיָ: For three sins of Israel, and for four, I will not forgive them: they went so far as to sell innocent people for money, and the needy in order to gain possessions.

qualifications.he: עַד דְזַבִּינוּ נמסר כלשון הגעה עד למעשה: חטאיהם הגיעו עד מכירת הזכאים והנזקקים. עד אינו מוחלף בעל, ואין כאן תנאי של חידוש הסליחה לאחר המכירה. בְּדִיל דְיַחֲסְנוּן מציין תכלית של השגת קניין, בלי מושא מפורש המזהה אותו כרכוש הנמכרים. רש״י מצטט במפורש את לשון התרגום ומציע ב'ואומר אני' הסבר של רכישת שדה בידי דיינים; פרטי ההצעה אינם מתווספים לתרגום. אין במקור הארמי אזכור לנעליים.
qualifications.en: עַד דְזַבִּינוּ is rendered as reaching the point of an act: their sins went so far as selling the innocent and needy. עַד is not replaced by עַל, and this is not a condition under which forgiveness resumes after the sale. בְּדִיל דְיַחֲסְנוּן expresses the purpose of gaining possessions, without an explicit object identifying them as the victims' property. Rashi explicitly quotes the Targum wording and, with 'וְאוֹמֵר אֲנִי', proposes an explanation involving judges acquiring a field; those additional details are not added to the translation. The Aramaic source does not mention shoes.
qualifications.anchor: עַד דְזַבִּינוּ בְּכַסְפָּא זַכָּאִין וַחֲשִׁיכַיָא בְּדִיל דְיַחֲסְנוּן

pairs.fullEnglish: And it happened on the third day, Pharaoh's birthday, that he made a feast for all his servants; and he remembered the head of the chief of the cupbearers and the head of the chief of the bakers among his servants.

qualifications.he: בֵּית וַלְדָא נקרא כאן כצירוף המציין את מאורע הלידה או חגיגתו; דְפַרְעֹה מייחס את המאורע לפרעה. מכאן התרגום 'יום הולדת פרעה', בלי להוסיף לידת בן בביתו. רש״י על העברית מפרש 'יוֹם לֵידָתוֹ' וקורא לו 'יוֹם גֵּינוּסְיָא'; זו תמיכה מקבילה בזיהוי המאורע, ולא ציטוט מפורש שלו לפירוש מילות התרגום. אין כאן קביעה של מנהגי החגיגה מעבר למשתה הכתוב.
qualifications.en: בֵּית וַלְדָא is read here as a compound naming the birth occasion or its celebration; דְפַרְעֹה assigns that occasion to Pharaoh. Hence 'Pharaoh's birthday,' without adding the birth of a son in his household. Rashi on the Hebrew explains 'יוֹם לֵידָתוֹ' and calls it 'יוֹם גֵּינוּסְיָא'; this is parallel support for identifying the occasion, not an explicit quotation by him explaining the Aramaic words. No celebration customs beyond the stated feast are asserted.

pairs.fullEnglish: And it happened, when he drew back his hand, that, behold, his brother came out; and she said, ‘What great strength you have to prevail!’ And he called his name פָּרֶץ.

qualifications.he: הקריאה היא קריאת התפעלות על כוחו הרב של הנולד: תְקוֹף הוא הכוח, סַגִּי מציין את ריבויו, עֲלָךְ מייחס אותו למי שאליו פונים, ולְמִתְקָף מתאר את ההתגברות שלשמה עומד הכוח. ׳להתגבר׳ שומר את לשון התרגום בלי להוסיף פריצת פתח, מכשול מסוים או יריב שלא נאמרו בו. רש״י מפרש את ׳פרצת׳ העברי ׳חָזַקְתָּ עָלֶיךָ חֹזֶק׳; זו השוואה ללשון הכוח ולא העתקה של דימוי הפרץ. וּקְרָא הוא פועל זכר, ולכן נמסר ׳הוא קרא׳ בלי להוסיף את שמו של הקורא.
qualifications.en: The exclamation concerns the newborn's great strength: תְקוֹף is strength, סַגִּי marks its greatness, עֲלָךְ attributes it to the person addressed, and לְמִתְקָף describes the prevailing for which that strength serves. ‘Prevail’ preserves the Targum's strength language without adding a breached opening, a particular obstacle or an unnamed opponent. Rashi explains the Hebrew פרצת as חָזַקְתָּ עָלֶיךָ חֹזֶק; this is a comparison supporting strength language, not a substitution of the Hebrew breach image. וּקְרָא is masculine, so ‘he called’ is retained without supplying the caller's name.

pairs.fullEnglish: For matters carried out from before יְיָ אֱלֹהִים do not succeed unless He has revealed His secret to His servants the prophets.

qualifications.he: כָשְׁרִין מתפרש כאן על הצלחתם של הדברים: הם אינם מצליחים אלא אם גילה את סודו לעבדיו הנביאים. אין זה ניסוח של דין כשרות הלכתי, וגם לא החלפה של תיאור ההצלחה בטענה שהדברים כלל אינם נעשים. מִן קֳדָם נשמר כלשון ׳מלפני׳, ואֱלָהִין מציין את תנאי הגילוי.
qualifications.en: כָשְׁרִין is rendered here in terms of the matters' success: they do not succeed unless He has revealed His secret to His servants the prophets. This is not a ruling on ritual validity, nor is successful outcome replaced by the claim that the matters do not occur at all. מִן קֳדָם is retained as 'from before', and אֱלָהִין introduces the revelation condition.
qualifications.anchor: אֲרֵי לָא כָשְׁרִין פִּתְגָמִין דְמִתְעַבְּדִין מִן קֳדָם יְיָ אֱלֹהִים אֱלָהִין גְלָא רָזֵיהּ

pairs.fullEnglish: And Israel loved Joseph more than all his sons, because he was a wise son to him; and he made him a striped tunic.

qualifications.he: התרגום 'כותונת בעלת פסים' משקף כאן את המובן הארמי 'רצועה, פס', שיאסטרוב מדגים במפורש בתרגום אונקלוס לבראשית לז:ג ולז:כג. אין בכך קביעה כיצד נוצרו הפסים, מהו חומר הבגד או עד כמה הוא עדין, אילו צבעים היו בו, אם נוספה לו עבודת עיטור, או מה היו גזרתו ואורך שרווליו. לביטוי העברי נמסרו גם פירושים של אריג עדין ושל שרוולים המגיעים עד פרקי הידיים; התרגום כאן נשען על העדות המילונית הארמית ואינו מכריע בין אותם פירושים עבריים.
qualifications.en: ‘Striped tunic’ here reflects the Aramaic sense ‘strip, stripe,’ which Jastrow expressly illustrates with Onkelos at Genesis 37:3 and 37:23. This does not specify how the strips or stripes were formed, the fabric's material or fineness, any particular colors, added decorative work, or the garment's cut or sleeve length. Fine-cloth and wrist-reaching-sleeve interpretations are also recorded for the Hebrew garment expression; the translation here follows the Aramaic lexical evidence without deciding among those Hebrew interpretations.

pairs.fullEnglish: And they reclined around to eat bread, and they raised their eyes and saw, and behold, a caravan of Arabs was coming from גִּלְעָד, and their camels were carrying wax, balsam, and aromatic resin, going to take them down to Egypt.

qualifications.he: שלושת השמות מונים מוצרי משא נפרדים, ואין לצמצם את כולם ל׳בשמים׳. שְׁעַף נמסר כשעווה, לפי הייחוס המפורש של תרגום שעווה לאונקלוס בפירוש רש״י כאן; קְטַף נמסר כצרי, מוצר של הפרשה צמחית; לְטוֹם נמסר כשרף ריחני, לפי הערך במילון יאסטרוב המציין את הפסוק הזה בתרגום. אלה זיהויים של סוגי חומר, לא קביעה של מין בוטני מודרני, הרכב מדויק או אופן הכנה. פירוש שורש העשב המובא ברש״י למילה העברית אינו מועתק כהגדרה של השם הארמי לְטוֹם.
qualifications.en: The three nouns enumerate separate cargo products and must not all be collapsed into 'spices'. שְׁעַף is given as wax, following Rashi's express attribution of a wax rendering to Onkelos here; קְטַף is given as balsam, a plant-exudate product; לְטוֹם is given as aromatic resin, following Jastrow's entry citing this Targum passage. These are material-class renderings, not identifications of a modern botanical species, exact composition, or preparation. The herb-root explanation Rashi reports for the Hebrew word is not transferred as a definition of the Aramaic noun לְטוֹם.

pairs.fullEnglish: And they sent the striped tunic, and they brought it to their father and said, ‘This we found. Recognize now whether it is your son's tunic or not.’

qualifications.he: התרגום 'כותונת בעלת פסים' משקף כאן את המובן הארמי 'רצועה, פס', שיאסטרוב מדגים במפורש בתרגום אונקלוס לבראשית לז:ג ולז:כג. אין בכך קביעה כיצד נוצרו הפסים, מהו חומר הבגד או עד כמה הוא עדין, אילו צבעים היו בו, אם נוספה לו עבודת עיטור, או מה היו גזרתו ואורך שרווליו. לביטוי העברי נמסרו גם פירושים של אריג עדין ושל שרוולים המגיעים עד פרקי הידיים; התרגום כאן נשען על העדות המילונית הארמית ואינו מכריע בין אותם פירושים עבריים.

This does not specify how the strips or stripes were formed, the fabric's material or fineness, any particular colors, added decorative work, or the garment's cut or sleeve length. Fine-cloth and wrist-reaching-sleeve interpretations are also recorded for the Hebrew garment expression; the translation here follows the Aramaic lexical evidence without deciding among those Hebrew interpretations.

pairs.fullEnglish: And it happened, when Joseph came to his brothers, that they stripped Joseph of his tunic, the striped tunic that was upon him.

qualifications.he: התרגום 'כותונת בעלת פסים' משקף כאן את המובן הארמי 'רצועה, פס', שיאסטרוב מדגים במפורש בתרגום אונקלוס לבראשית לז:ג ולז:כג. אין בכך קביעה כיצד נוצרו הפסים, מהו חומר הבגד או עד כמה הוא עדין, אילו צבעים היו בו, אם נוספה לו עבודת עיטור, או מה היו גזרתו ואורך שרווליו. לביטוי העברי נמסרו גם פירושים של אריג עדין ושל שרוולים המגיעים עד פרקי הידיים; התרגום כאן נשען על העדות המילונית הארמית ואינו מכריע בין אותם פירושים עבריים.
qualifications.en: ‘Striped tunic’ here reflects the Aramaic sense ‘strip, stripe,’ which Jastrow expressly illustrates with Onkelos at Genesis 37:3 and 37:23. This does not specify how the strips or stripes were formed, the fabric's material or fineness, any particular colors, added decorative work, or the garment's cut or sleeve length. Fine-cloth and wrist-reaching-sleeve interpretations are also recorded for the Hebrew garment expression; the translation here follows the Aramaic lexical evidence without deciding among those Hebrew interpretations.

dayTitle.en: Joseph in his father's household and the beginning of hatred

explanation.he: אונקלוס מתאר את יוסף כבן חכם לאביו, ולא רק כבן שנולד לעת זקנה. הוא גם מתרגם שהאחים לא רצו לדבר עמו לשלום; סיפור החלום מוסיף על שנאתם.
explanation.en: Onkelos describes Joseph as a wise son to his father, rather than merely a son born in old age. He also says that the brothers were unwilling to speak peaceably with him; the telling of the dream adds to their hatred.

dayTitle.en: The sheaves and the stars in Joseph's dreams

explanation.he: החלום הראשון מתאר את אלומת יוסף עומדת ואת אלומות אחיו משתחוות לה. בדברי האחים אונקלוס מפרש את שאלת המלוכה בלשון מחשבה וציפייה לשלטון, ואילו האב גוער ביוסף לאחר סיפור החלום השני.
explanation.en: The first dream describes Joseph's sheaf standing upright and his brothers' sheaves bowing to it. In the brothers' response, Onkelos expresses the question of kingship in terms of imagining and expecting dominion, while the father rebukes Joseph after the second dream is told.

dayTitle.en: Joseph is sent to his brothers

explanation.he: האחים מקנאים ביוסף, ואביו שומר את הדבר בלבו. האב שולח אותו לברר את שלום אחיו ואת שלום הצאן; אונקלוס מציין את מישור חברון כמקום שממנו נשלח.
explanation.en: The brothers are jealous of Joseph, while his father keeps the matter in mind. The father sends him to inquire into the welfare of his brothers and of the flock; Onkelos identifies the plain of Hebron as the place from which he was sent.

dayTitle.en: The plot against Joseph and Reuben's intervention

explanation.he: יוסף מוסיף ללכת אחרי אחיו עד דותן. האחים מתכננים להמיתו ולתלות את היעלמותו בחיה רעה, וראובן מתערב ואומר שלא להמיתו.
explanation.en: Joseph continues after his brothers as far as דֹתָן. The brothers plan to kill him and attribute his disappearance to an evil beast, and Reuben intervenes by saying not to take his life.

dayTitle.en: The pit and the question of profit from a brother's death

explanation.he: הכתוב בתרגומו של אונקלוס מציין במפורש שראובן מבקש להציל את יוסף ולהשיבו לאביו. לאחר השלכת יוסף לבור נראית שיירת ערבים, ויהודה שואל על התועלת הכספית שבהריגת אחיהם.
explanation.en: The supplied Onkelos explicitly states that Reuben intends to rescue Joseph and return him to his father. After Joseph is thrown into the pit, a caravan of Arabs appears, and Judah asks what monetary benefit there would be in killing their brother.

dayTitle.he: מכירת יוסף ותחילת מעשה יהודה ותמר
dayTitle.en: Joseph's sale and the beginning of Judah and Tamar's story

explanation.he: אונקלוס מתאר את יוסף כנמכר לערבים ואת יעקב כמסרב לקבל תנחומים. בהמשך הוא מכנה את אבי אשת יהודה סוחר, ומפרש שהזרע שאונן נמנע מלהקים לא ייקרא על שמו. תמר יושבת בדרך לתמנת לאחר שראתה ששלה גדל והיא לא ניתנה לו לאישה.
explanation.en: Onkelos describes Joseph as sold to Arabs and Jacob as refusing to receive consolation. He then calls the father of Judah's wife a merchant and explains that the offspring אוֹנָן refuses to raise up would not be called by his own name. Tamar sits on the road to תִּמְנָת after seeing that שֵׁלָה has grown up and she has not been given to him as a wife.

dayTitle.he: הכרת יהודה, ניסיונו של יוסף ופתרון החלומות
dayTitle.en: Judah's recognition, Joseph's trial, and the interpretation of dreams

explanation.he: יהודה מכיר בחפצים ואומר שתמר זכאית ושהיא הרה ממנו. בסיפור יוסף חוזר אונקלוס על כך שמימרא של יי מסייעת לו, והוא מפרש את כניסתו לבית כבדיקת ספרי חשבונותיו. בבית האסורים נעשה הכול על פי דבר יוסף; הוא מייחס את פתרונות החלומות למקורם מלפני יי, אך שר המשקים שוכח אותו לאחר השבתו לתפקיד.
explanation.en: Judah recognizes the objects and says that Tamar is in the right and is pregnant by him. In Joseph's story, Onkelos repeatedly states that the Word of יְיָ is his help and explains his entry into the house as an examination of his account books. In the prison everything is done at Joseph's word; he attributes dream interpretations to their source before יְיָ, but the chief cupbearer forgets him after being restored to office.

dayTitle.en: Oppression of the Needy and Divine Kindness

explanation.he: התרגום מונה מכירת זכאים, הטיית דין וחילול השם לצד ניצול משכונות וסחיטה. כנגד המעשים האלה ניצבים הכרתת האמורי, היציאה ממצרים וההנהגה במדבר. הוא מזכיר גם הקמת נביאים ומלמדים מבני ישראל.
explanation.en: The Targum lists the sale of innocent people, perverted judgment, and profanation of the holy name alongside the abuse of pledges and extortion. Against these acts stand the destruction of the Amorite, the departure from Egypt, and guidance through the wilderness. It also recalls the raising up of prophets and teachers from Israel's own children.

dayTitle.en: Words of Truth Worth More Than Gold

explanation.he: החכמה מתארת את דבריה כאמת וצדקות שאין בהן פיתול או עיקום. דבריה גלויים למתבונן וישרים למבקשי ידיעה. משום כך היא קוראת לקבל מוסר ולבחור בידיעה יותר מבכסף, בזהב ובאבנים טובות.
explanation.en: Wisdom describes its words as truth and righteousness without twisting or crookedness. They are clear to the understanding person and upright to those who desire knowledge. It therefore calls for accepting discipline and choosing knowledge above silver, gold, and precious stones.

dayTitle.en: Silenced Prophecy and the Loss of Escape

explanation.he: ישראל מתוארים כמי שהטעו את מלמדיהם ביין וציוו על הנביאים שלא להתנבא. העקה הבאה נמשלת ללחצה של עגלה טעונת עמיר. קלות רגליים, כוח, קשת וסוסים אינם מספקים הצלה באזהרה הזאת.
explanation.en: Israel is described as leading its teachers astray with wine and ordering the prophets not to prophesy. The coming distress is compared to the pressure of a cart loaded with sheaves. Swiftness, strength, a bow, and horses provide no escape in this warning.

dayTitle.en: Wisdom, Hatred of Evil, and Righteous Rule

explanation.he: החכמה קושרת את יראת ה׳ לשנאת הרע, הגאווה והפה ההפוך. היא מייחסת לעצמה מחשבה, עצה, הבנה וגבורה. בתיאור השלטון היא אומרת שמלכים מולכים בזכותה ושהיא מושחת שליטים בצדקות.
explanation.en: Wisdom connects fear of יְיָ with hatred of evil, pride, and perverse speech. It claims thoughtful purpose, counsel, understanding, and might as its own. In describing government, it says that kings reign because of it and that it anoints rulers in righteousness.

dayTitle.he: בחירה, אחריות וסימנים שיש להם סיבה
dayTitle.en: Divine Favor, Accountability, and Signs with Causes

explanation.he: האזהרה פותחת בבריחת גיבור בלי נשק וממשיכה בפנייה אל המשפחות שהועלו ממצרים. דווקא הרצון המיוחד בישראל נקשר לפקידת כל חובותיהם. שאלות ההליכה המשותפת ושאגת האריה מציגות מעשים וסימנים שאינם באים בלי דבר הקודם להם.
explanation.en: The warning begins with a mighty man's flight without weapons and continues by addressing the families brought up from Egypt. The special delight taken in Israel is linked to the visitation of all its sins. The questions about walking together and a lion's roar present acts and signs that do not occur without something preceding them.

dayTitle.en: Wisdom Before the Depths, Mountains, and Heavens

explanation.he: החכמה מתארת את בריאתה וכינונה לפני מעשי הבריאה ולפני היות הארץ. עומקים, מעיינות, הרים וגבעות נמנים בתיאור הקדימה הזאת. כשהשמים מתכוננים ומעגל נחקק על פני התהום, היא אומרת שהיתה שם.
explanation.en: Wisdom describes its creation and establishment before the works of creation and before the earth came to be. Depths, springs, mountains, and hills appear in this account of its precedence. When the heavens are established and a circle is traced over the deep, it says that it was there.

dayTitle.he: אותות אזהרה, גילוי הסוד ועושק בשומרון
dayTitle.en: Warning Signs, Revealed Secrets, and Oppression in Samaria

explanation.he: שאלת הציפור והמלכודת ותקיעת השופר מחוץ לזמנו ממשיכות את רצף אותות האזהרה. התרגום תולה את כשרין של הדברים הנעשים מלפני ה׳ בגילוי סודו לעבדיו הנביאים; לא הוכרע כאן אם כשרין מתייחס להתגשמות הדברים או לכשרותם ותקפותם. אחר כך הוא מדגיש את קבלת הנבואה ומזמין עדים לראות בשומרון מהומות, אנשים הנתונים לעושק ואוצרות המתמלאים מחטף וביזה, בניגוד לעשיית התורה.
explanation.en: The question about the bird and snare and the horn sounded outside its appointed time continue the sequence of warning signs. The Targum makes a condition of revealing God's secret to His servants the prophets for the matters done from before Him; whether its predicate כָשְׁרִין concerns their realization or their fitness and validity remains unsettled here. It then emphasizes receiving prophecy and summons witnesses to Samaria's disturbances, oppressed people, and treasuries filled with robbery and plunder rather than conduct according to the Torah.

dayTitle.en: The Fall of Dominion, the Altar, and Luxurious Houses

explanation.he: הנבואה מתארת עקה קשה, ביטול כוח וביזת ארמונות. משל הרועה המציל שתי כרעיים או סחוס אוזן מפי האריה מלווה את תיאור היושבים בשומרון בתוקף שלטון והבוטחים בדמשק. פקידת החטאים מגיעה לעובדי המזבחות בבית אל, וקרנות המזבח נכרתות ונופלות. גם בתי החורף, בתי הקיץ והבתים המעוטרים בשן פיל עתידים להיפגע; אין בתיאור פירוט של שיטת העיטור בשן.
explanation.en: The prophecy describes severe distress, the removal of might, and the plundering of palaces. The image of a shepherd rescuing two legs or ear cartilage from a lion accompanies the description of those dwelling in Samaria in the strength of rule and trusting in Damascus. The visitation of sins reaches those who serve the altars in Bais El, and the altar's horns are cut off and fall. The winter houses, summer houses, and houses adorned with elephant ivory also face destruction; the account does not specify the method of ivory embellishment.

dayTitle.en: Loving Wisdom, Its Fruit, and the Paths of Righteousness

explanation.he: החכמה אוהבת את אוהביה ונמצאת למקדימים אליה. עושר, כבוד, קניין, מזל וצדקה מיוחסים לה, ופירותיה מתוארים כטובים מזהב מזוקק וטהור. גם תבואתה נזכרת בהשוואה, אך המילים סניא גביא אינן מאפשרות כאן זיהוי בטוח של הדבר שאליו היא מושווית; אין לקבוע שהוא כסף. החכמה הולכת בדרכי צדקה ודין כדי להנחיל לאוהביה שנים רבות ולמלא את אוצרותיהם.
explanation.en: Wisdom loves those who love it and is found by those who come early to it. Wealth, honor, possessions, fortune, and righteousness belong to it, and its fruits are described as better than refined and pure gold. Its yield is also compared with something, but the words סַנְיָא גַבְיָא do not securely identify that comparison here; it cannot be stated as silver. Wisdom walks in ways of righteousness and judgment so as to cause its lovers to inherit many years and to fill their treasuries.

dayTitle.he: גבולות הבריאה, שמחת החכמה והקריאה לבנים
dayTitle.en: Creation's Boundaries, Wisdom's Joy, and the Call to Children

explanation.he: התיאור ממשיך בכינון העננים, חיזוק מעיינות התהום, גבול הים ויסודות הארץ. החכמה נמצאת לצד הבורא כנאמנת ושמחה לפניו בכל זמן. בתיאור השבח היומי שבפסוק ל לא ברור כאן אם היא מושא לשבח או מתוארת ביחס לדברי שבח. בהמשך היא שמחה בתבל ארצו, ושבחיה בין בני האדם בלי לקבוע מי משבח את מי. לבסוף היא קוראת לבנים לשמוע לה ומכריזה על אושרו של השומר את דרכיה.
explanation.en: The account continues with the establishing of clouds, the strengthening of the deep's springs, the sea's boundary, and the earth's foundations. Wisdom is at the Creator's side as a trusted one and rejoices before Him at all times. In the daily praise expression of verse 30, whether it is an object praised or is described in relation to words of praise remains unclear here. It then rejoices in His inhabited earth, with its praises among human beings, without specifying who praises whom. Finally it calls children to listen and declares the happiness of the one who keeps its ways.
